message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Deck** | 108 cards (4 colors × 25 cards each + 8 special cards per color) | | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or play all cards in a single round). | | **Setup** | Shuffle the deck; deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. | | **Turn Order** | Clockwise (unless altered by a Reverse card). | | **Gameplay** | On your turn you may play one card that matches either the color or the number/symbol of the top discard. If you cannot play, you must draw from the draw pile until you can play or the pile is empty. | | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes direction of play.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses a turn (must be played only if you have no matching color). | | **Calling “UNO”** | When you play your second‑to‑last card, shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. Failure to call UNO when required results in a penalty of drawing two cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The first player to discard all of their cards wins the round. | | **Scoring** | Winner scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards still held by opponents:
• Number cards = face value
• Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20 points each
• Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50 points each | | **Game End** | First player to reach 500 points (or agreed target) wins the game. | **Optional Variations** | Variation | Effect | |-----------|--------| | **Stacking** | Players may stack Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards on top of each other, forcing the next player to draw the cumulative total unless they also have a matching card. | | **No Wild Draw Four Rule** | Some groups forbid playing Wild Draw Four unless you truly have no playable card. | | **House Rules** | Many groups add house rules such as “draw two on a skip” or “reverse counts as a skip.” | **Key Strategy Tips** 1. **Keep a mix of colors** – Having multiple colors reduces the chance you’ll be stuck with a single color at the end. 2. **Save Wilds for the end** – Wild cards are high‑value points; holding them until the end can give you a big advantage. 3. **Watch the discard pile** – Pay attention to what cards are being played; it gives clues about opponents’ hands. 4. **Use Draw Two/Reverse strategically** – Force opponents to draw or change direction when you’re close to winning. That’s the core of Uno! Feel free to tweak or add house rules to suit your group.
